calls.head: Quinn gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Capitals keep sending Wilson’s line (Protas, Jenner and Wilson) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Spencer Carbery has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Sabres’ first line is Benson, Östlund and Quinn.

calls.head: The Capitals’ edge in depth
calls.body: The Capitals are near the top of the league for depth, and the Sabres are near the bottom. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Capitals spread their forward ice time deeper down the lineup than the Sabres.

surprises.head: Buffalo leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: Buffalo usually uses their bottom six less than most teams. Not tonight: the bottom six played 48% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 41% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 450 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Tuch sparks a Capitals comeback
paras: Jack Quinn and Josh Doan scored just over four minutes apart early in the first to put the Sabres up 2-0. Alex Tuch got the Capitals on the board late in the period, in his first game against Buffalo since leaving. Dylan Strome tied it 2-2 early in the second, and he struck again late in the period to put the Caps ahead 3-2. Noah Östlund made it 3-3 for Buffalo early in the third. Tuch won it with his second goal of the night in overtime. Strome added an assist for a three-point night.

The Capitals owned the chances, outshooting the Sabres 34-21, and still had to sweat it out in overtime. The Sabres hit a post and the crossbar and still lost. Charlie Lindgren made 18 saves for the Capitals, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 30 of 34 at the other end. The Capitals improved to 6-4-0 and climbed to fourth in the Metropolitan, while the Sabres fell to 4-4-3, still last in the Atlantic.
